title: Threat Model Sorter
description: A threat model lists what could go wrong and decides what to fix first. Here each classroom threat has a likelihood and an impact from 1 to 3, and the risk score is their product. Threats are fixed from the highest score down; equal scores put the cheaper fix first, and a final tie goes to the lower threat number, so the order is unique.
creator: Dan McCreary

learningObjectives: The learner will prioritize 10 classroom threats into the correct fix order using each threat's likelihood, impact, and effort to fix, with at least 8 of 10 threats in the correct position.
prerequisites: threat model, asset, actor, attack surface, likelihood, impact, risk score, effort to fix (all defined in the section "The Threat Model" above this block).

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Explore, then fixed-order practice items with one attempt each and immediate explained feedback
keyQuestions: Is the most technical-sounding threat always the most important?
Why does effort decide the order of the six threats that tie at 6?
Is a threat caused by our own bug a real threat?
commonMisconceptions: (1) The most technical-sounding threat is always the most important. (2) Likelihood alone decides priority. (3) Equal scores mean the order does not matter. (4) A threat caused by our own bug is not a real threat.
assessmentOpportunities: Submit one order. Mastery is 8 of 10 threats in the correct position.
